transcript: Nothing makes me go absolutely feral with anticipation and nothing gets me to fly across the Atlantic Ocean quite like a game of theater Mad Libs where you take great actors, great directors, great material and just play a fun game of mix and match with them. So of course I lost my goddamn mind when I saw this absolutely stacked lineup of actors and creatives working on one of my favorite classic plays. But did the actual show live up to my ridiculously high expectations and hopes? No. No, I would say it didn't. It was a bit of a mixed bag to be honest. On the positive side, the performances were for the most part, everything I'd hoped they'd be. Kate Blanchett as Irina reminded me of like that kooky acting professor we all had who really wants to be seen as this like, eccentric free spirit, but then weaponizes that as an excuse to be invasive and cruel. Emma Corrin and Tom Burke also delivered really strong performances, but actually for me the biggest highlight was Tanya Reynolds, who I mostly know from Sex Education. I thought she was fantastic as Masha. But the weakest link for me by far, unfortunately, was Oscar nominee Cody Smith Mcphee as Constantine, who I thought was really awkward and wooden in this performance. I think they were going for like, brooding and withdrawn, but it. It just did not read properly at all. And I. I think even if it had Not sure I would have liked it, cause it felt like a very humorless rendition of what I think is a tragic comic role. And of course, the production was directed by Thomas Ostermeier, who's like one of the most prominent experimental theater directors in Europe. I loved his productions of hamlet and Richard the third, but this one felt honestly kind of tamed to me. There were some choices I really liked, but I wanted more of them and more from them. It felt a little half hearted, a little incohesive. And even though I loved most of the performances individually, as an ensemble, I don't think they were particularly connected to each other. But you know, folks, I started off by calling this a game of theater Mad Libs. And like in a real game of Mad Libs, sometimes you pick a great adjectives and great nouns, and it's just not that funny when you read it out loud in the end, you know, that's the risky take. And I'm happy to keep playing the game. And maybe it's just the copium talking, but I have no regrets.
